elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence opens: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Kubient shall...", covering both expiry and any termination.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause commits only to "transition assistance for at least ninety (90) days"; no six-month period appears in operative language (six months is mentioned only in the margin comment).

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: No pricing basis is stated for the assistance; "then-current rates" appears nowhere in the inserted text.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination export and deliver to Customer all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer (including Requests)" — return obligation with the 30-day anchor tied to expiry/termination.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: The export obligation specifies no format; "commonly used, machine-readable format" is absent from the operative sentence.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion-and-certification obligation follows the export; retained Section 4(c)(iv) only requires return or destruction of Confidential Information, with no written certification and no sequencing after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason" — both triggers expressly covered, and the assistance period runs "following such expiry or termination", so it is not limited to anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "provide transition assistance for at least ninety (90) days following such expiry or termination"; the "at Customer's request" condition is general and applies to every covered exit event, not only anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination export and deliver to Customer all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer (including Requests)" — the data trigger covers every category of Customer data, not selected named types, and runs from termination rather than from a request.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: all three elements are carried by a single inserted sentence with the correct triggers (expiry or termination), the correct duration floor (at least 90 days), and the correct 30-day export anchor measured from expiry/termination rather than from a request.

Preferred level is not reached: the operative text lacks a six-month assistance period, a then-current-rates charging basis, a machine-readable format requirement, and a post-return certified deletion obligation. These are only referenced in the margin comment, which is not operative.

Minimality holds. The insertion is a single concise sentence in the termination-effects provision, adds no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no procedures or boilerplate, and deletes nothing from Section 4(c)(i)-(iv). The parenthetical "(including Requests)" is a necessary anchor because the Agreement defines no "Customer Data" term, so it clarifies rather than expands the checklist.

Intent is preserved: cessation of Services, licence revocation, cease-use and mutual Confidential Information return/destruction all survive unchanged, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling.

Optional hardening (not required at the fallback target): retained Section 4(c)(iv) lets each Party "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information, which could be read to permit destruction of AP data before export. If the drafter wants belt-and-braces, prefix the new sentence with "Notwithstanding Section 4(c)(iv)," rather than editing the retained clause.
